turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): alright, before the doctor comes in I'm just gonna check your pressure. arm out for me, palm up.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): oh yeah sure, of course. I rolled the sleeve in the waiting room already, these offices are always chilly so my hands get cold, hope that doesn't throw the number off.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): you're fine. 128 over 78, pulse 76, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): 128, okay. the pharmacy machine said something like 150 over whatever last spring when I was late, but that was months ago and I don't count it.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): mm. he'll be right in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll sit over here, I drove her. her husband's pills are in a different bag so nobody mixes them, he takes metformin, a thousand milligrams, and those aren't hers.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): hey, I'm Dr. Patel. what's been going on.

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): well, um, it's my stomach. err, I've been getting these cramps low down and they ease off once I pass stool, plus the bloating, and my bowels have been switching around for about a year.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): okay, let me get that. cramps that settle after a bowel movement, bloating, bowels changing for about a year. what does the switching actually look like.

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): so some days I'm constipated, I sit there and nothing happens. then other days it's loose and kind of urgent, I have to find a bathroom, and it goes back and forth. I even keep a note in my phone, not perfect, but most weeks I write something down.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): she's been on about it at home since last year, yeah. and she skips lunch when the meetings stack up.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): any blood in the stool?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): no. no blood. I check, I know it's not pleasant, but I look pretty much every time, and I have not seen blood on the paper or in the bowl.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): have you lost any weight?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): no, I haven't lost weight. the scale at home is the same, I weigh myself Sunday mornings, and the number hasn't dropped. the jeans feel tight when I'm bloated but that's the bloat, not a real change on the scale.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): alright, no blood and no weight loss. how often are the cramps, and where do you feel them.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): most days, uh, five days a week, especially after lunch. they sit low, both sides but more the left, and once I go they fade. not sharp like a knife, more a crampy squeeze that kind of rolls.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): and the bloating, what sets that off.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): stress, honestly, and big meals. work has been a lot, I'm a project coordinator at a logistics company and the deadlines pile up, and when I'm stressed the bloating gets worse. I skip lunch when meetings run long and then I eat a huge one, which doesn't help. I don't smoke, and I'll have a glass of wine on a weekend sometimes, that's it.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): so work stress and large meals make the bloating worse, and lunch is hit or miss. are you taking anything for the bowels?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): umm, myralax, the powder. one cap in water, a couple times a week, only when I can't go, not every day. I tried imodium once when it was loose and it bunged me up, so I left that alone.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): one cap of MiraLAX a couple times a week for constipation, and you stopped the Imodium after a single try. any other medicines that are actually yours?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): no, that's the only thing I take. my sister keeps telling me to try biotin, she takes 5000 micrograms, those gummies, for her hair. I don't take biotin, that's her thing, not mine, even though she texts me about it constantly.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): biotin stays your sister's. any drug reactions, anything you've ever reacted to?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): no, never. I have taken penicillin and everything. amoxicillin when I had strep a few years back, the whole course, and I was fine, no rash, no swelling, nothing.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): no reactions, including a penicillin-type antibiotic. outside the gut, any trouble with urination?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): no, peeing is totally normal. no burning, I go a regular amount, that's never been the problem, it's all the bowels and the cramping.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): okay. I'm going to feel your belly, if that's alright.

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah go ahead. I had a bagel this morning so it might be a little full, sorry. the sore spot is usually the left lower bit, I can point if you need, it's about where my hand is now.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): soft. tender on the left lower side when I press. no guarding.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah that's the spot, that's exactly where the cramp sits. it eases when you let go, same as after I use the bathroom. I've poked it myself at home which probably isn't useful but it feels the same.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): she holds that left side in the car sometimes. I wasn't sure if I should even mention it.

[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): it matches what I'm finding, so yes, worth saying. let me put it together. about a year of crampy lower pain that gets better after you pass stool, bloating worse with stress and big meals, constipation and loose stools alternating, no bleeding, no weight loss. this sounds like it could be irritable bowel, and that's my working impression, not a final label.

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): irritable bowel, okay. I've read about that online at midnight, which I know is a bad idea, and some of it fit and some of it scared me. I wanted an actual person to say it instead of a webpage.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): understandable. I'm going to order bloodwork today, a blood count and a celiac screen, so we're not missing something that can look similar.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): blood count and the celiac one, okay. err, do I need to fast, because I already ate the bagel, and if I have to come back I can do tomorrow morning before work, I start at eight.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): no fasting for these. on food, smaller meals, add fiber gradually, not all at once, and keep that phone note going. ease off the huge lunches when you can.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): smaller meals, fiber slow, keep the note, I can do that. the fiber thing, like oats or a powder, because the powder makes me more gassy if I jump up too fast, I learned that in a meeting once, very embarrassing. so food first is better for me.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): food first, oats, fruit, not a big jump in any powder. we might do a ct scan of the belly if it does not settle. I'm not booking that today.

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): a scan only if it doesn't settle, okay. I'd rather not unless we need it, those machines make me a little claustrophobic if I'm honest. if you say later that we should, I will.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): let's see you back in two weeks with the blood results and the food note. reception can put that on the schedule on your way out.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): two weeks, yeah. I'll bring the note, and I'll try not to google the whole time. thanks, really, both of you.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

omissions.text: Abdominal pain was described as low down on both sides but worse on the left, and as 'crampy/squeezing/rolling' rather than sharp.
Urgency with loose stools was reported ('kind of urgent, I have to find a bathroom').
Negative urinary findings were more specific: no burning with urination and normal urine amount/frequency ('peeing is totally normal').
No other personal medicines besides MiraLAX were reported; caregiver clarified metformin 1000 mg belongs to the husband and is not the patient's medication.
The patient specifically does not take biotin; the 5000 microgram biotin gummies mentioned belong to her sister, not the patient.
Allergy history was more explicit: she reported no drug reactions and specifically tolerated amoxicillin/penicillin previously with no rash or swelling.
Planned follow-up included returning in two weeks with both the blood results and the food/phone note.
